newsitem.title: HAITI: Haitian mob protests on anniversary of coup.
newsitem.headline: Haitian mob protests on anniversary of coup.

text.p: Mobs of noisy demonstrators burned hundreds of tires in the streets in a protest seeking justice against those who carried out a brutal military coup against then-president Jean-Bertrand Aristide five years ago on Monday.

The protesters expressed frustration with a justice system so far unable to punish the coup leaders. "President Rene Preval is not going after the people who killed so many," said protester Victor Sieve.

U.N. peacekeepers were on alert, with some kneeling on the front lawn of the National Palace and guns pointed at the protestors. "We're on a general alert, to make sure no one enters the palace perimeter," said one Canadian peacekeeper.

About 5,000 people were killed in three years under the military regime that led the coup. That regime was ousted in September 1994 by a peaceful U.S.-led intervention, and upon his return, Aristide disbanded the Haitian army.
But this summer the ex-soldiers have been angrily protesting and are suspected to have carried out attacks last month in Port-au-Prince.

There were renewed fears about those who took power five years ago when Radio Haiti-Inter reported on Monday that an ex-military leader, Joseph Jean Baptiste, was arrested over the weekend in connection with a plot to launch another coup.
Baptiste was a leader of the Committee for Soldiers Demands, which has threatened violence if the former soldiers' demands for back pay and a pension are not met.

Radio Haiti-Inter reported the arrest was related to a cache of guns found at the home of Emmanuel "Toto" Constant, a leader of the now-defunct paramilitary group. That group, the Revolutionary Front for the Advancement and Progress of Haiti, is believed to have carried out most of the violence while the military was in power.

Constant currently lives in New York and was ordered to refrain from political activities as part of an agreement that freed him from a U.S. prison, where he was incarcerated by immigration officials when his visa expired.
The Radio Haiti report said police found evidence that the guns found at Constant's house were to be used by ex-soldiers in a new attempt to overthrow the government.
U.N. troops outside the palace said they were not warned of any alleged plot by ex-soldiers to target Preval or other government officials.
